newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece's new two-year T-bill set at 10.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Greece's new two-year T-bill set at 10.3 pct.

text.p: Greece will issue new two-year zero coupon T-bills on January 20th at a rate of 10.3 percent, Deputy Finance Minister Nickos Christodoulakis told reporters.
It will be the first time Greece has issued a two-year zero-coupon T-bill as it has accustomed the market to shorter- term three, six and 12-month T-bills.

"The new debt security is available to the entire investment public but mainly to retail investors who will now be able to replace their 12-month T-bills with a similar security of a longer maturity," the finance ministry said.
Interest earned on the new two-year T-bills is subject to tax of 7.5 percent upon maturity.

"Given the economy's positive developments, reflected in the recent credit rating upgrade by Moody's Investors Services and the continuing fall in inflation and interest rates, investors who opt for these securities benefit by a fixed return for the next two years," it said.

To illustrate, investors who buy a new two-year T-bill with a par value of 1.0 million drachmas will pay 821,957 and receive a net 986,647 drachmas in two years after a tax deduction of 13,353 drachmas, the ministry said.

A one million drachma two-year T-bill will thus pay interest of 178,043 drachmas before tax. Interest earned during the first year is capitalised. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
